nodes.name: Marxism–Leninism
nodes.desc: Revolutionary branch of Marxism that advocates the seizure of power by a vanguard party and the dictatorship of the proletariat, with a planned economy and collectivization, serving as the foundation of the communist regimes of the 20th century.

nodes.name: Stalinist Socialism
nodes.desc: Soviet model consolidated by Stalin, marked by accelerated industrialization, agricultural collectivization, rigid central planning, personalized leadership and mass political repression.

nodes.name: Maoist Communism
nodes.desc: Mao's Chinese adaptation of Marxism, centered on the peasantry as the revolutionary force, protracted people's war, permanent mass mobilization, and cultural revolution against the party bureaucracy.

nodes.name: Trotskyist Communism
nodes.desc: Current of Trotsky, co-founder of the Soviet state and the Red Army, which defends permanent revolution, a vanguard party and the dictatorship of the proletariat, criticizing Stalinist bureaucracy without renouncing one-party rule.

nodes.name: Luxemburgist Socialism
nodes.desc: Democratic Marxism inspired by Rosa Luxemburg, which unites revolution and freedom, values the spontaneity of the masses and the general strike, and criticizes both reformism and the authoritarian centralism of vanguard parties.

nodes.name: National Communism
nodes.desc: Current that combines a planned socialist economy with a strong national identity, prioritizing the sovereignty and interests of its own country over internationalism, often under personalist and centralized leadership.

nodes.name: Juche Socialism
nodes.desc: North Korean doctrine formulated by Kim Il-sung that combines state socialism, national self-reliance, single-party rule, supreme leadership, militarization and rejection of external dependence, subordinating economy and society to the sovereignty of the regime.

nodes.name: Pol Pot Socialism
nodes.desc: Radical agrarian communism of the Khmer Rouge that emptied cities, abolished money and markets, and pursued an egalitarian peasant society by force, causing one of the greatest genocides of the 20th century in Cambodia.

nodes.name: Dengist Socialism
nodes.desc: Pragmatic reform initiated by Deng Xiaoping that introduced markets, private property, and economic opening under the absolute control of the Communist Party, forming the model of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

nodes.name: State Socialism
nodes.desc: System in which the state controls the means of production and directs the economy through central planning, promoting industrialization and welfare under strong political authority and limited popular democratic participation.

nodes.name: Authoritarian Progressivism
nodes.desc: Project that imposes progressive social transformations from above, using state power to accelerate changes in customs and equality, even at the cost of individual liberties and organized political opposition.

nodes.name: Eco-Authoritarianism
nodes.desc: Current that advocates a strong, interventionist state to confront the environmental crisis, subordinating economic and political freedoms to ecological urgency and strict control of consumption and production.

nodes.name: Left-Wing Technocracy
nodes.desc: Model that combines socialist planning with scientific management of the economy, entrusting expert committees, rather than elections or party competition, with the rational organization of production and the egalitarian distribution of society's resources.

nodes.name: National Bolshevism (NazBol)
nodes.desc: Syncretic ideology, also called NazBol, that fuses revolutionary socialism and radical nationalism, combining a collectivist economy, state authoritarianism, and rejection of liberalism, the West, and bourgeois individualism.

nodes.name: Strasserist Socialism
nodes.desc: Anti-capitalist wing of National Socialism, linked to Gregor Strasser, which emphasized a mass nationalist socialism, nationalization, and social revolution within the movement, later crushed by Hitler.

nodes.name: Fascism
nodes.desc: Ultranationalist doctrine of national rebirth that rejects liberalism and Marxism, exalts the totalitarian state and the leadership of a single chief, sees action and violence as a means of regeneration, and treats the nation as a secular religion, with variants beyond the Italian regime that gave it its name.

nodes.name: National Socialism
nodes.desc: German variant of fascism based on racism, antisemitism, and expansionism, which united totalitarianism, the cult of Hitler, and the idea of a superior race, culminating in World War II and the Holocaust.

nodes.name: Falangism
nodes.desc: Spanish authoritarian nationalism of Catholic and syndicalist inspiration, created by José Antonio Primo de Rivera on the corporatism of his father Miguel's dictatorship; it defends a corporatist state, national unity and social hierarchy, and was a pillar of Francoism.

nodes.name: National Syndicalism
nodes.desc: Nationalist and syndicalist current that rejects liberalism and Marxism, advocating national unity, corporatist organization of labor, authoritarian social justice, and popular mobilization around the state.

nodes.name: Brazilian Integralism
nodes.desc: Authoritarian nationalist movement that arose in 1930s Brazil, Christian and corporatist, with the motto God, Fatherland and Family, a mass aesthetic and opposition to liberalism and communism.

nodes.name: Authoritarian Capitalism
nodes.desc: Model that combines a market economy and private property with a closed political regime, in which the state guarantees order, growth, and stability while restricting civil liberties and political competition.

nodes.name: National Capitalism
nodes.desc: System that unites free enterprise with strong protectionism and state direction, prioritizing industry, jobs, and national sovereignty over global free trade and unchecked foreign capital.

nodes.name: Radical Right
nodes.desc: Radical right movement born on the internet, combining identitarian nationalism, opposition to immigration and multiculturalism, criticism of globalism and provocative rhetoric. Part of its voices defend a nationalism based on race.

nodes.name: Alt-Lite
nodes.desc: Branch of the radical right that is nationalist and anti-globalist, emphasizing cultural identity, criticism of immigration and opposition to political correctness, without adopting race-based positions.

nodes.name: Right-Wing Accelerationism
nodes.desc: Current that defends accelerating the system's contradictions through technology and the weakening of liberal institutions, betting on a break with the existing order to give rise to a new hierarchical social and political order.

nodes.name: Neoconservatism
nodes.desc: Right-wing current that unites free markets, traditional values, and an interventionist foreign policy, advocating the promotion of democracy and national interests through military force and global leadership.

nodes.name: Absolute Monarchism
nodes.desc: Defense of monarchy with unlimited power concentrated in the sovereign, legitimized by tradition or divine right, without a constitution or parliament to restrict the king's authority over state and society.

nodes.name: Authoritarian Conservatism
nodes.desc: Current that preserves order, tradition, and hierarchy through a strong state, restricting freedoms and political participation in the name of social stability, morality, religion, and established authority.

nodes.name: National Conservatism
nodes.desc: Current that unites traditional values, family, and religion with strong cultural nationalism, defending sovereignty, borders, and the people's identity within democracy, with clear distrust of globalism.

nodes.name: Paternalistic Conservatism
nodes.desc: Conservative tradition that accepts social reforms and protection for the poorest to preserve national cohesion, seeing elites as responsible for the people's welfare and for harmony between classes.

nodes.name: Religious Fundamentalism
nodes.desc: Project that seeks to organize state and society according to the strict interpretation of a religious doctrine, subordinating laws, customs, and politics to sacred precepts and rejecting modern secularism.

nodes.name: Ethnic Nationalism
nodes.desc: Conception that defines the nation by shared origin, language and descent, defending a state for the majority ethnic group and the preservation of its identity, which usually implies membership criteria tied to ancestry.

nodes.name: Cultural Nationalism
nodes.desc: Nationalism based on shared language, traditions, and heritage rather than race, which values the people's cultural identity and the integration of those who adopt these values, defending the nation's cohesion.

nodes.name: Neoreaction
nodes.desc: Current that rejects modern democracy and egalitarianism and proposes replacing them with hierarchical, efficient governments run like companies by a sovereign, combining traditionalism and technology.

nodes.name: Cameralism
nodes.desc: Administrative doctrine of enlightened absolutism that organized the state through a disciplined bureaucracy and centralized finances, promoting industry, population, and revenue as sources of the monarch's power.

nodes.name: Corporatism
nodes.desc: Model that organizes society into corporations of workers and employers integrated into the state, seeking harmony between classes and directed economic cooperation instead of conflict or free competition.

nodes.name: Reactionaryism
nodes.desc: Stance that rejects modernity and seeks to restore the pre-revolutionary order, defending monarchy, religion, tradition, and hierarchy against Enlightenment rationalism, liberalism, and democracy.

nodes.name: Fourth Political Theory
nodes.desc: Theory by Aleksandr Dugin that rejects liberalism, communism, and fascism and proposes a multipolar world founded on civilizations, tradition, and collective identity, opposing globalism and Western hegemony.

nodes.name: National Democracy
nodes.desc: Current that combines popular sovereignty and democratic institutions with strong cultural nationalism, prioritizing the nation's interests and identity over supranational commitments and multiculturalism.

nodes.name: Bioconservatism
nodes.desc: Position that opposes genetic manipulation and the technological enhancement of the human body, defending ethical limits on science in the name of dignity, human nature, and prudence toward the future.

nodes.name: Right-Wing Technocracy
nodes.desc: Model that entrusts the management of the state and the economy to experts and technological efficiency, combining markets, innovation, and technical decisions instead of political deliberation and traditional party competition.

nodes.name: Christian Democracy
nodes.desc: Centrist current that applies Christian values to democratic politics, defending the social market economy, family, solidarity, and the common good as the foundation of free and pluralist institutions.

nodes.name: Christian Conservatism
nodes.desc: Current that grounds politics in Christian morality and tradition, defending family, life, and religious values within democracy, with emphasis on preserving the people's customs and cultural heritage.

nodes.name: Republicanism
nodes.desc: Political tradition that values popular sovereignty, civic virtue, and the rule of law, defending citizens' self-government, the separation of powers, and protection against tyranny and the corruption of power.

nodes.name: Constitutional Monarchism
nodes.desc: Defense of monarchy as a symbol of unity and continuity, with the king subject to the constitution and parliament, uniting tradition and institutional stability with representative democracy and the rule of law.

nodes.name: Neoliberalism
nodes.desc: Current that advocates free markets, deregulation, privatization, and fiscal discipline, reducing the state's economic role and trusting competition and monetary stability as engines of prosperity.

nodes.name: Ordoliberalism
nodes.desc: German liberal school of Freiburg (Eucken, Rüstow, Müller-Armack) that defends the free market within firm rules guaranteed by the state, against monopolies and central planning, with a Christian ethical basis and social policy, the origin of the social market economy.

nodes.name: Distributism
nodes.desc: Doctrine of Christian inspiration that advocates the wide distribution of property and small-scale production, opposing both monopoly capitalism and state socialism in favor of autonomous communities.

nodes.name: Technocracy
nodes.desc: Model of government in which decisions are made by experts and technical, scientific criteria, entrusting engineers, economists, and scientists with the rational and efficient management of the state and the economy.

nodes.name: Communitarianism
nodes.desc: Current that values community bonds, traditions, and the common good above individualism, holding that justice and identity arise from life in community and the responsibilities people share.

nodes.name: Liberalism
nodes.desc: Political tradition that places individual freedom at the center, defending rights, tolerance, the rule of law, a market economy, and limits on power, with government subject to the consent of citizens.

nodes.name: Classical Liberalism
nodes.desc: Original branch of liberalism that defends natural rights, property, free markets, and a minimal state, seeing individual freedom and the strict limitation of power as the foundations of a just society.

nodes.name: Libertarianism
nodes.desc: Philosophy that advocates maximum individual freedom and a state reduced to essential functions, valuing private property, free markets, and personal autonomy while rejecting state coercion over life.

nodes.name: Green Liberalism
nodes.desc: Current that unites individual freedom, markets, and democracy with the ecological agenda, defending sustainability, rights, and innovation to reconcile economic prosperity with effective environmental protection.

nodes.name: Social Liberalism
nodes.desc: Branch that combines individual freedoms with strong state action to guarantee welfare, education, and healthcare, defending equal opportunity and social security within the market economy.

nodes.name: Conservative Liberalism
nodes.desc: Synthesis that unites free markets and economic freedoms with the appreciation of tradition, order, and institutions, defending prudent change and social stability within the framework of liberal democracy.

nodes.name: Geolibertarianism
nodes.desc: Synthesis of libertarianism and Georgism that combines free markets and individual freedoms with the taxation of land value, seen as a common resource, to fund the minimal state without punishing labor.

nodes.name: State Liberalism
nodes.desc: Liberal current that accepts an active role for the state in the economy and in guaranteeing rights, combining individual freedoms and markets with regulation and public policies aimed at the collective good and equality.

nodes.name: Environmentalism
nodes.desc: Movement dedicated to protecting the environment and the sustainable use of resources, advocating policies against pollution and climate change and harmony between human development and ecological balance.

nodes.name: Conservatism
nodes.desc: Political tradition that values order, customs, family, and consolidated institutions, preferring gradual and prudent change over rupture, based on historical experience and skepticism toward utopias.

nodes.name: Progressivism
nodes.desc: Current that advocates social reforms and the expansion of rights to promote equality and justice, trusting progress, science, and collective action to transform institutions and overcome inequalities.

nodes.name: Nationalism
nodes.desc: Ideology that places the nation as the central value, defending its sovereignty, unity, and identity, and prioritizing the interests of the people and the nation-state over external influences and globalism.

nodes.name: Civic Nationalism
nodes.desc: Nationalism based on citizenship and shared values rather than ethnicity, defining the nation by adherence to common laws and institutions, open to all who accept its democratic and civic principles.

nodes.name: Indigenism
nodes.desc: Current that values indigenous peoples and their rights, defending autonomy, territory, culture, and political participation, along with development models and a plurinational state that respect their traditions.

nodes.name: Socialist Conservatism
nodes.desc: Current that unites a socialist economy with traditional values, defending social protection and a strong state role alongside family, order, and customs, far from the cultural progressivism of liberal lefts.

nodes.name: Anarchism
nodes.desc: Philosophy that rejects the state and all coercive authority, defending the free organization of society through voluntary associations, cooperation, and self-management, with freedom and equality as central values.

nodes.name: Anarcho-Communism
nodes.desc: Current that unites anarchism and communism, proposing a society without state or private property, with collective production and distribution according to need, based on free association and mutual aid.

nodes.name: Anarcho-Syndicalism
nodes.desc: Current that sees revolutionary unions as the basis for overthrowing capitalism through direct action and the general strike, organizing production by the workers themselves in a free, stateless society.

nodes.name: Syndicalism
nodes.desc: Movement that places unions and workers' organization at the center of politics, defending collective bargaining, direct action, and labor control over production as the path to working-class emancipation.

nodes.name: Libertarian Socialism
nodes.desc: Current that pursues socialism without an authoritarian state, uniting collective ownership and self-management with broad individual freedom, organized from the bottom up by free communities and workers.

nodes.name: Market Socialism
nodes.desc: System in which collectively or publicly owned enterprises compete in markets, uniting the efficiency of competition with the socialist distribution of profits, without the rigid central planning of state economies.

nodes.name: Mutualism
nodes.desc: Anarchist current founded by Proudhon that advocates fair exchange, free credit, and use-based property, with producers and cooperatives trading among themselves without exploitation, bosses, or a central state.

nodes.name: Minarcho-Mutualism
nodes.desc: Synthesis that unites mutualism with a minimal state, combining fair exchange, cooperatives, and free credit with a public structure reduced to the essential functions of protecting rights, contracts, and freedoms.

nodes.name: Communalism
nodes.desc: Model created by Murray Bookchin based on autonomous municipalities and federated popular assemblies, with a community economy and direct democracy, seeking to replace the state with a free confederation.

nodes.name: Christian Socialism
nodes.desc: Current of Thomas Müntzer, the peasants of 1525 and priests such as Camilo Torres, which seeks the Kingdom of God on Earth through revolution, with common property and power in the hands of the poor.

nodes.name: Christian Labourism
nodes.desc: Branch that combines the defense of workers and social justice with Christian values, promoting labor rights, solidarity, and social protection within democracy, inspired by the social doctrine of the Church.

nodes.name: Christian Social Democracy
nodes.desc: Current that turns the Gospel into reforms within democracy, defending a welfare state, labor rights, unions and redistribution without breaking with the market or with liberal institutions.

nodes.name: Social Democracy
nodes.desc: Current that seeks to reconcile capitalism and social justice through democracy, defending regulated markets, a strong welfare state, labor rights, and redistribution to reduce social inequalities.

nodes.name: Socialism
nodes.desc: Broad doctrine that advocates social or collective ownership of the means of production and economic planning to overcome capitalist exploitation, accepting both the revolutionary and the reformist road to get there.

nodes.name: Liberal Socialism
nodes.desc: Current that unites socialist goals of equality and social justice with the defense of individual freedoms and democracy, combining strong social protection with pluralism, civil rights, and a mixed economy.

nodes.name: Social Libertarianism
nodes.desc: Left-libertarian branch that unites broad individual freedom with collective or shared ownership of resources, defending autonomy, cooperation, and the rejection of both the authoritarian state and capital.

nodes.name: Eco-Socialism
nodes.desc: Current that fuses socialism and ecology, attributing the environmental crisis to capitalism and defending collective, sustainable, and democratic production that respects the limits of nature and social needs.

nodes.name: Deep Ecology
nodes.desc: Current that attributes intrinsic value to all life and not only to human beings, defending a profound change of values, the reduction of human impact, and respect for the balance of the planet's ecosystems.

nodes.name: Agrarian Anarchism
nodes.desc: Anarchist branch centered on the countryside, defending autonomous rural communities, collective ownership of land, and peasant cooperation, rejecting the state and land concentration in favor of self-management.

nodes.name: Green Anarchism
nodes.desc: Current that unites anarchism and radical ecology, defending decentralized, sustainable communities without a state or exploitation of nature, in harmony with ecological cycles and non-human life.

nodes.name: Anarcho-Progressivism
nodes.desc: Synthesis of anarchist currents centered on the liberation of body and identity, uniting the critique of patriarchy and of gender and sexuality norms with an openness to technology as a tool of emancipation, all under the rejection of the state, capitalism, and every imposed hierarchy.

nodes.name: Anarcho-Pacifism
nodes.desc: Anarchist branch that rejects the state and all violence, defending social transformation through nonviolent means, civil disobedience, and voluntary cooperation as the path to a free and just society.

nodes.name: Christian Anarchism
nodes.desc: Current that unites Christian faith with anarchism, holding that the Gospel preaches love, equality, and nonviolence incompatible with the state, and defending free communities based on conscience and charity.

nodes.name: Anarcho-Naturism
nodes.desc: Anarchist branch linked to naturism that defends simple living in contact with nature, without a state or oppressive conventions, valuing individual autonomy, health, and harmony with the natural world.

nodes.name: Geoanarchism
nodes.desc: Synthesis of anarchism and Georgism that rejects the state but treats land and natural resources as commons, defending that their rent be shared by the whole community in a free and egalitarian way.

nodes.name: Anarcho-Capitalism
nodes.desc: Current that proposes abolishing the state and organizing all of society through contracts and free markets, with security, justice, and services provided by competing private companies under absolute property rights.

nodes.name: Minarchism
nodes.desc: Libertarian branch that defends a minimal state limited to police, courts, and defense, leaving everything else to the market and private initiative, to protect individual rights without oppressing freedom.

nodes.name: Paleolibertarianism
nodes.desc: Branch that combines radical free markets with traditional, conservative cultural values, defending economic freedom, property, and autonomous local communities against the state and progressivism.

nodes.name: Hoppean Libertarianism
nodes.desc: Current tied to Hans-Hermann Hoppe that joins anarcho-capitalism, absolute private property and criticism of democracy, defending social orders based on contract, voluntary association and private authority.

nodes.name: Capitalism
nodes.desc: Economic system based on private property, free markets, and the pursuit of profit, in which production and prices are regulated by competition and supply and demand, with individual initiative as its engine.

nodes.name: Objectivism
nodes.desc: Philosophy created by Ayn Rand that exalts reason, individualism, and rational egoism, defending laissez-faire capitalism and the pursuit of one's own happiness as the supreme moral purpose of each person's life.

nodes.name: Eco-Capitalism
nodes.desc: Current that seeks to solve the environmental crisis through the market, using pricing, green technology, and incentives to make protecting nature profitable and compatible with growth and free enterprise.

nodes.name: Eco-Conservatism
nodes.desc: Branch that unites conservatism and environmental protection, defending the preservation of nature as part of the tradition and heritage to be passed on to future generations, with prudence toward change.

nodes.name: Eco-Nationalism
nodes.desc: Current that links environmental protection to national sovereignty, prioritizing the protection of the country's own natural resources and land and sustainable development within national borders.

nodes.name: Crypto-Anarchism
nodes.desc: Current that uses cryptography and digital technologies to guarantee privacy, freedom, and transactions beyond state control, seeking to weaken surveillance and authority through technological means.

nodes.name: Bleeding-Heart Libertarianism
nodes.desc: Current that unites free markets and individual freedoms with concern for social justice, holding that economic freedom must also concretely improve the lives of the poorest and most vulnerable.

nodes.name: National Libertarianism
nodes.desc: Branch that combines the defense of individual freedoms and free markets with appreciation for national sovereignty and identity, defending limited government alongside border control and the nation.

nodes.name: Libertarian Monarchism
nodes.desc: Current that sees monarchy as a guarantee of freedom and stability, defending a king with limited power who protects property and individual rights and maintains a lean, minimally interventionist state.

nodes.name: Federalist Monarchism
nodes.desc: Current advocating a monarch who actually governs, as constitutional head of the executive or absolute sovereign, over a federation of states or regions with broad self-government, as in the German Empire of 1871, the United Arab Emirates, and Malaysia.

nodes.name: Libertarian Conservatism
nodes.desc: Synthesis that unites free markets and a minimal state with the defense of tradition, family, and order, valuing individual freedom and personal responsibility alongside the preservation of customs and institutions.

nodes.name: Progressive Libertarianism
nodes.desc: Branch that pursues gender equality through individual freedom and the market rather than the state, defending autonomy, equal rights, and the end of legal restrictions on women's choices.

nodes.name: Anarcho-Conservatism
nodes.desc: Current that rejects the state but preserves tradition, religion, and community values, defending a spontaneous social order based on customs, family, and natural authority instead of central political power.

nodes.name: Anarcho-Distributism
nodes.desc: Synthesis of anarchism and distributism that defends the wide distribution of property and small-scale production, with autonomous communities and cooperatives organized without a state or large monopolies.

nodes.name: Centrism
nodes.desc: Political position that seeks balance between left and right, valuing moderation, pragmatism, and consensus, and combining elements of different currents to avoid extremes and favor gradual reforms.

nodes.name: Labourism
nodes.desc: Current that defends workers' interests within democracy, promoting labor rights, social security, strong unions, and income distribution through reforms and the welfare state.

nodes.name: Positivism
nodes.desc: Current inspired by Auguste Comte that trusts science and reason to organize society, defending order, progress, and technical administration guided by knowledge in place of metaphysics and tradition.

nodes.name: Secular Conservatism
nodes.desc: Conservative branch that defends order, tradition, and institutions without grounding them in religion, supporting cultural values and social stability with secular, historical, and pragmatic arguments.

nodes.name: Christian Progressivism
nodes.desc: Current that unites Christian faith with the defense of social justice, rights, and reforms, seeing in the Gospel a call to solidarity, equality, and care for the poor and marginalized of society and the world.

nodes.name: Modernizing Authoritarianism
nodes.desc: Model inspired by Park Chung-hee's regime, combining state-led industrialization, credit for private firms, and planning with anti-communist political repression.

nodes.name: State Developmentalism
nodes.desc: Model in which the state directs industrialization and economic growth through planning, public investment, and industrial protection, seeking to overcome the nation's backwardness and external dependence.

nodes.name: Atlanticism
nodes.desc: Geopolitical doctrine of the alliance between the US, Canada and Europe around NATO and the EU, which backs the alliance's eastward expansion and the use of Western military power to spread liberal democracy and free markets against Russia and China.

nodes.name: Techno-Monarchism
nodes.desc: A unitary variant of neoreaction: an absolute CEO-monarch rules a centralized state through data and security technology (surveillance, AI), under market capitalism, private property and free enterprise, for the sake of stability and efficiency.

nodes.name: Right-Wing Progressivism
nodes.desc: Right-wing progressive branch that unites capitalism and the cult of technological progress with a socially progressive, pragmatic, and secular culture, entrusting society's direction to a technical elite rather than mass democracy.

nodes.name: Techno-Socialism
nodes.desc: Current that joins the dictatorship of the proletariat with technological accelerationism, defending a revolutionary party, data-driven planning, automation, and collective ownership to lead the transition to communism.

nodes.name: Techno-Fascism
nodes.desc: Current that joins the totalitarian authoritarianism of fascism to digital surveillance, artificial intelligence and technological control of the population, using technique to secure order and national unity.

nodes.name: Authoritarian Liberalism
nodes.desc: Current that combines a market economy, private property, trade openness, and technocracy with low democratic participation, holding that a strong, efficient state should preserve order, stability, and growth.

nodes.name: Progressive Nationalism
nodes.desc: Current that unites national sovereignty, economic protection, and popular integration with progressive social reforms, seeking a state capable of defending the nation while expanding rights, equality, and inclusion.

nodes.name: Eco-Fascism
nodes.desc: Current that joins radical ecology, authoritarianism and organic nationalism, defending population control, environmental preservation imposed by the state and the subordination of individual liberties to the survival of the national community.

nodes.name: Agrarian Communism
nodes.desc: Revolutionary model that idealizes peasant life and collective rural production, rejecting cities, markets, and private property in favor of an equality imposed by state mobilization and communal discipline.

nodes.name: Bolivarian Socialism
nodes.desc: Latin American project that combines popular nationalism, anti-imperialism, social redistribution, and strong presidential leadership, using the state and strategic resources to promote sovereignty and popular inclusion.

nodes.name: National Developmentalism
nodes.desc: Current that advocates industrialization, national sovereignty, and strategic state planning, seeking to modernize the economy through public investment, productive protection, and coordination between government, science, and national companies.

nodes.name: Libertarian Populism
nodes.desc: Branch that unites anti-politics, radical free markets, and direct popular communication, attacking bureaucracies, taxes, and party elites in the name of individual freedom, entrepreneurship, and the sovereignty of the ordinary citizen.

nodes.name: Christian Theocratism
nodes.desc: Christian theocratist doctrine that subordinates political power to religious authority, holding that divine law and the Church should govern the state and customs, from medieval and papal ultramontanism to modern reconstructionist projects.

nodes.name: Titoist Socialism
nodes.desc: Variant of socialism developed in Tito's Yugoslavia, combining single-party rule and a cult of the leader with workers' self-management of enterprises, federal decentralization, market openness, and non-alignment between the Cold War blocs.

nodes.name: Anti-Colonial Socialism
nodes.desc: Socialist current born of national liberation struggles in Africa, Asia, and Latin America, defending economic sovereignty, resource nationalization, non-alignment, and solidarity among peoples of the Global South against imperialism.

nodes.name: Techno-Communism
nodes.desc: Current that combines the final stage of communism with technological acceleration, using automation and AI to overcome scarcity, necessary labor, and private property.

nodes.name: Techno-Anarchism
nodes.desc: Technological anarchism that proposes abolishing the state through automation, abundant energy, decentralized networks, and self-managed voluntary communities with digital tools and free local production.

nodes.name: Christian Accelerationism
nodes.desc: Current that fuses traditional Christianity with technological acceleration, holding that artificial intelligence, industry and national power should be driven forward unchecked as a civilisational mission against secular decay.

nodes.name: Right-Wing Populism
nodes.desc: Current that mobilizes the people against political and cultural elites, combining nationalism, immigration restriction, traditional values, public religion, strong security, and anti-establishment economic pragmatism around personalist leaders.

nodes.name: Left-Wing Populism
nodes.desc: Current that mobilizes the people against economic elites, defending redistribution, public control, national sovereignty, plebiscitary democracy, and broad social policy in popular anti-establishment language.

nodes.name: Social Centrism
nodes.desc: Centrist branch that accepts the market economy but prioritizes social protection, public services, gradual reforms, and institutional consensus to reduce inequality without political rupture or permanent polarization.

nodes.name: Liberal Centrism
nodes.desc: Pro-market centrist branch that combines fiscal responsibility, liberal democracy, moderate international openness, and institutional reform, rejecting both broad statism and libertarian radicalism as a political program.

nodes.name: Green Centrism
nodes.desc: Centrist branch that prioritizes sustainability, gradual energy transition, environmental regulation, and technological prudence, seeking to reconcile climate protection, markets, and democratic institutions without anti-capitalist rupture.

nodes.name: Conservative Centrism
nodes.desc: Centrist branch that combines economic moderation and institutional respect with social conservatism, valuing family, religion, order, and gradual change without joining the authoritarian right or populist radicalism.

nodes.name: National Liberalism
nodes.desc: Right-wing current that combines free markets, free trade, and limited government with strong national identity, cultural assimilation, traditional and religious values, and a robust military.

nodes.name: Archeofuturism
nodes.desc: A doctrine coined by Guillaume Faye that fuses archaic, hierarchical and traditionalist values — ethnic identity, spirituality and a warrior ethos — with an unreserved embrace of advanced technology, arguing that an approaching civilizational collapse will force humanity to combine tribal social order with hyper-modern science.

nodes.name: Pragmatism
nodes.desc: Political stance that judges proposals by the practical results they produce rather than fidelity to an ideological dogma, combining market measures, regulation, and social policy according to evidence and each problem's context.

nodes.name: Right-Wing Pragmatism
nodes.desc: Pragmatic branch that prioritizes fiscal adjustment, economic stability, and governability through broad coalitions, accepting market reforms and political concessions in the name of short- and medium-term results.

nodes.name: Left-Wing Pragmatism
nodes.desc: Branch that seeks concrete social results by negotiating with the market and existing institutions, prioritizing responsible fiscal austerity, targeted social policy, and governability over revolutionary ideological purity.

nodes.name: Imperialism
nodes.desc: Doctrine that defends the territorial, military and economic expansion of a nation over other peoples and territories, keeping colonies and spheres of influence tied to the interests of the metropole through military and political power.

nodes.name: Progressive Liberalism
nodes.desc: Current that unites market capitalism and globalized trade with a robust welfare state, advocating progressive morality, secularism, and democratic institutions, in the Nordic social model.

nodes.name: Militarism
nodes.desc: Regime centered on the armed forces as the core of political power, governing by junta or military hierarchy, with centralization, discipline, a high value on order and expansionism, and civilian politics subordinate to military command.

nodes.name: Federalism
nodes.desc: Doctrine that organizes the state through a constitutional division of power between a central government and autonomous regional units, such as cantons or states, with their own competencies, independent courts, and mutual checks against excessive concentration of power.

nodes.name: Left Accelerationism
nodes.desc: A post-capitalist techno-socialist synthesis accelerating AI, automation, and cybernetics to reduce compulsory work, socialize abundance, and plan an economy beyond capital; it combines universalism and decommodification with radically progressive social transformation.

nodes.name: American Conservatism
nodes.desc: Platform of the Republican Party, combining border security and deportations, tariffs and industrial protectionism, tax cuts and deregulation, gun rights, Christian values and returning abortion to the states.

nodes.name: Securitarian Democracy
nodes.desc: Militant democracy doctrine, authorizing a democratic state to restrict the enemies of democracy itself by banning anti-system parties, monitoring extremists and maintaining conscription and reinforced security to defend the constitutional order.

nodes.name: Armed Pacifism
nodes.desc: Armed neutrality that refuses alliances, interventions and foreign projection, yet sustains robust armed forces, compulsory service and prepared territorial defense, treating military strength as the guarantee of not being dragged into other nations wars.

nodes.name: Progressive Theocracy
nodes.desc: Theocracy led by clerical authority without popular sovereignty, which establishes from above a progressive morality as a divine commandment: gender equality, sexual liberation, sacred ecology and a break with inherited custom, seen as superstition to be reformed.

nodes.name: Traditionalist Atheism
nodes.desc: Thoroughly secular conservatism that rejects faith and clergy while defending hierarchy, family, authority, nation and inherited customs as civilizational goods, treating traditional morality as a social necessity rather than a divine commandment.

nodes.name: Mercantilism
nodes.desc: Doctrine combining free enterprise and competition in the domestic market with an external tariff wall, subsidies for infant industry, a national bank, public infrastructure and trade surplus as a source of national power.

nodes.name: Pluralist Imperialism
nodes.desc: Autocratic, militarized imperial order that expands territory by conquest yet governs conquered peoples through communal autonomy, administered religious tolerance and tribute, without demanding cultural assimilation from its subjects.

nodes.name: Federalist Imperialism
nodes.desc: Project of a dynastic empire organized as a federation of nationalities, with regional autonomy, local parliaments and recognized languages, while retaining a hereditary crown, unified army and military assertion of imperial greatness.

nodes.name: Aristotelianism
nodes.desc: Aristotle's political philosophy, defending a mixed constitution of monarchical, aristocratic and popular elements to avoid both tyranny and radical democracy, reserving full citizenship for those with virtue, property and the education to deliberate.

nodes.name: Financial Monarchism
nodes.desc: Dynastic microstate model that trades political sovereignty for prosperity: a hereditary prince with real power, minimal taxation, secrecy and financial services as the revenue base, openness to foreign capital and residents, and no standing army.

nodes.name: Aristocratic Liberalism
nodes.desc: Liberalism before mass democracy: it guarantees civil liberty, property, a free press and a lean state, but restricts the vote to educated property owners, fearing that unlimited popular sovereignty would destroy the very liberties it protects.

nodes.name: Libertarian Authoritarianism
nodes.desc: A doctrine separating political authority from social control: it favours concentrated, unelected executive power insulated from popular vote, which in exchange guarantees civil liberty, privacy and minimal state interference in private life and morals.

nodes.name: Jacobin Liberalism
nodes.desc: A current that sees the unitary, centralized state as the guarantor of individual liberty: uniform law, secularism and single citizenship dismantle the local, clerical and corporate privileges that would oppress the individual without a strong national power.

nodes.name: Libertarian Militarism
nodes.desc: A doctrine combining a minimal state in taxation, regulation and morals with strong armed forces and an armed citizenry: national defense is the one expanded state function, treated as the condition of civil liberty rather than its exception.

nodes.name: Zapatismo
nodes.desc: Neo-Zapatista movement that emerged in 1994 in southern Mexico, combining indigenous autonomy, direct democracy through assemblies and caracoles, cooperative subsistence economy, and refusal to seize state power, summed up as 'lead by obeying'.

nodes.name: Revolutionary Syndicalism
nodes.desc: Current that rejects the parliamentary and reformist path, betting on the general strike and the mobilising myth: direct union action and proletarian violence should destroy the state and the decadent bourgeoisie.

nodes.name: Confucianism
nodes.desc: Doctrine that grounds political order in the ruler's virtue, ritual hierarchy and filial piety, favouring bureaucratic merit and moral education over coercive law or popular participation.

nodes.name: Lassallean Socialism
nodes.desc: Socialist current that seeks to emancipate workers through the national state itself, with universal suffrage, producer cooperatives funded by public money and an explicit refusal of the revolutionary path.

nodes.name: Liberal Developmentalism
nodes.desc: The East Asian Tiger model (Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong): champions free markets, foreign trade and private enterprise as engines of growth, paired with an active technocratic state that plans infrastructure, education and strategic industrialization, stopping short of closed protectionism or hard authoritarian control.

nodes.name: Aristocratism
nodes.desc: Doctrine of rule by the best, which entrusts power to a minority qualified by virtue, education or birth, rejecting political equality and majority rule, which it sees as a risk to competence.

nodes.name: Nietzschean Aristocratism
nodes.desc: Nietzschean current that rejects egalitarian morality as herd resentment, defending a hierarchy of values, the aristocratic creation of meaning and the tragic affirmation of life after the death of God.

nodes.name: Catholicism
nodes.desc: Social doctrine of the Catholic Church, combining traditionalist morality and defense of life with concern for social justice, subsidiarity and worker dignity, under the hierarchical authority of the papacy and canon law.

nodes.name: Moderating Monarchism
nodes.desc: Nineteenth-century constitutional monarchy model in which the monarch exercises a fourth Moderating Power above the Executive, Legislative and Judiciary, arbitrating conflicts and guaranteeing stability over an agrarian economy.

nodes.name: Proudhonian Mutualism
nodes.desc: Proudhon's original doctrine, denouncing property as theft and advocating free mutual credit, federalism of autonomous communities and possession by use, with strong moral reservations about progress and customs.

nodes.name: Kantian Republicanism
nodes.desc: Kant's political philosophy, grounding the state's legitimacy in the autonomy of reason and the rule of law, defending a moderate representative republicanism and a federation of free states as the path to perpetual peace.

nodes.name: Socratism
nodes.desc: Socrates' dialectical method, examining beliefs through rational questioning and the pursuit of virtue, distrustful of mass politics and the rhetoric of demagogues, yet respectful of the city's rule of law.

nodes.name: Marxist Socialism
nodes.desc: Marx's original doctrine, analyzing history as class struggle and predicting capitalism's overcoming through proletarian revolution, with abolition of private ownership of the means of production and strong criticism of religion.

nodes.name: Platonism
nodes.desc: Plato's political philosophy, entrusting the city's government to a philosophical elite formed by virtue and knowledge, with strong control over education, property and customs in the name of justice and social harmony.

nodes.name: Athenian Democracy
nodes.desc: Ideology of the classical polis, advocating direct popular sovereignty through assembly and sortition among equal citizens, while reserving citizenship to a hereditary minority, excluding women, foreigners and slaves.

nodes.name: Nordic Social Democracy
nodes.desc: Scandinavian model combining tripartite collective bargaining among unions, employers and the state, a universalist welfare state funded by high taxes, and an open, export-driven market economy, with strong social consensus and low inequality.

nodes.name: Communism
nodes.desc: Final stage theorized by Marx and Engels: a classless, stateless society without private ownership of the means of production, with collective production and distribution according to need, superseding capitalism and the transitional socialist phase.

nodes.name: Liberal Technocracy
nodes.desc: Synthesis of the Asian Tigers: entrusts government to a merit-recruited technical elite insulated from the vote and guided by results rather than doctrine, combining free trade, open markets and low taxation with strict public order and state planning where it proves effective.

nodes.name: Peronist Nationalism
nodes.desc: Justicialist doctrine of Juan and Eva Perón uniting political sovereignty, economic independence and social justice, with CGT unions, nationalizations, protected industrialization, social Catholicism and a charismatic leader above parties.

nodes.name: Red Fascism
nodes.desc: Regime that fuses fascism's authoritarian aesthetics and hierarchy, with a strong leader, order and national discipline, to a socialist economy of collectivization, nationalized enterprise and central planning of the means of production.

nodes.name: Stoicism
nodes.desc: Greco-Roman philosophy that teaches living according to reason and nature, accepting with serenity what lies beyond one's control, cultivating duty, self-mastery and virtue above pleasure, and recognizing a natural law common to all rational humanity.

nodes.name: Agrarianism
nodes.desc: Republican tradition that idealizes the small landowning farmer as the basis of civic virtue and liberty, advocating wide distribution of land, limited and decentralized government, and distrust of banks, public debt, industry and large cities.

nodes.name: Utopian Socialism
nodes.desc: Early 19th-century current that envisioned an industrial society reorganized by rational planning, led by scientists, engineers and producers, replacing politicians and aristocrats without appealing to class struggle or revolution.

nodes.name: Techno-Commercialism
nodes.desc: A neoreactionary current that rejects democracy in favor of microstates run like firms. It favors competition among jurisdictions, free markets, the right of exit, and technological innovation as principles of government.

nodes.name: Neo-Thomism
nodes.desc: Revival of Thomas Aquinas's thought from 1879 (Leo XIII), with Maritain and Gilson. It grounds politics in natural law, the common good and subsidiarity, favoring mixed government, property with a social function and just war, under Catholic faith.

nodes.name: Eurasianism
nodes.desc: Russian geopolitical current that sees Eurasia as a distinct civilization and proposes a Moscow-led continental bloc, with regional autonomy and shared strategic command, against Atlanticism and US hegemony.

nodes.name: Democratic Socialism
nodes.desc: Current that seeks to move beyond capitalism through elections, with social ownership of large firms, cooperatives and workplace democracy, rejecting both the vanguard party and mere social democratic management of the market.

nodes.name: Third Way
nodes.desc: 1990s renewal of the center-left under Blair, Clinton and Giddens that accepts globalized markets and fiscal discipline, replaces welfare with work activation, is tough on crime and backs liberal interventions.

nodes.name: Paleoconservatism
nodes.desc: American traditionalist right, of Buchanan and Kirk, defending Christian heritage, localism and states' rights, immigration restriction, protectionism and non-interventionism, against neoconservatives and the managerial state.

nodes.name: Bonapartism
nodes.desc: Caesarist current that legitimises a charismatic leader by plebiscite above parties, combining personal authority, bureaucratic centralisation, military mobilisation and state-led modernising reforms.

nodes.name: Quilombism
nodes.desc: Political project developed by Abdias Nascimento from the history of Brazil's quilombos. It advocates racial equality, Afro-Brazilian self-determination, participatory democracy, a cooperative economy and land held for collective use.

nodes.name: Interventionist Democracy
nodes.desc: Foreign policy doctrine associated with the 2002 US strategy. It favours military force and preemptive action against threats, alongside the international promotion of democracy, open markets and US-led alliances.

nodes.name: Malthusian Environmentalism
nodes.desc: Environmental current inspired by Garrett Hardin that links population pressure to the depletion of common resources. It favours collectively enforced limits on resource use and policies to curb population growth.

nodes.name: Reaganite Conservatism
nodes.desc: American conservative current associated with Ronald Reagan. It combines lower taxes and a smaller federal economic role with free enterprise, traditional religious values, anticommunism and military strength.

nodes.name: Radical Centrism
nodes.desc: Centrism taken to its limit: it refuses any leaning on principle and seeks exact equidistance between every pole, from economics to morality, treating each political axis as a balance point to be preserved.

nodes.name: Political Buddhism
nodes.desc: Applies the Dharma to politics: Ashoka's righteous king, Schumacher's Buddhist economics, Buddhadasa's Dhammic socialism and Bhutan's Gross National Happiness. It prioritizes nonviolence, moderate consumption, community and harmony with nature.

nodes.name: Egoist Anarchism
nodes.desc: Current founded by Max Stirner in The Ego and Its Own (1844), which rejects the state, morality, religion and rights as spooks and proposes voluntary unions of egoists who associate only while it serves them.

nodes.name: Social-Developmentalism
nodes.desc: Model associated with Brazil's Workers' Party governments that seeks growth with social inclusion, combining rising minimum wages, popular credit, cash transfers and public banks without breaking with the market.

nodes.name: New Deal Liberalism
nodes.desc: Democratic Party current born with Franklin Roosevelt that joins financial regulation, social security, public works and strong unions with civic patriotism, preserved capitalism and international leadership.

nodes.name: Keynesian Liberalism
nodes.desc: Current inspired by John Maynard Keynes that accepts markets and liberal democracy but gives the state the task of managing demand, with countercyclical public spending, full employment as a goal and a mixed economy.

nodes.name: Brazilian Social Democracy
nodes.desc: Current of Brazil's PSDB, founded in 1988 by Covas, Montoro and Cardoso, joining a market economy, social state, state reform and fiscal responsibility with parliamentarism and moderation on social issues.

nodes.name: Varguist Nationalism
nodes.desc: Getúlio Vargas's Estado Novo doctrine joining economic nationalism, a centralized state, state-tied unions, labor law and state firms such as Petrobras, against the regional oligarchies and liberalism.

nodes.name: Cuban Socialism
nodes.desc: Revolutionary regime of Fidel Castro and Che Guevara, with a single party, a state-run economy, universal health and education, export of armed revolution and the new man ideal against imperialism.

nodes.name: African Socialism
nodes.desc: Current of Sankara, Samora Machel, Nkrumah and Nyerere joining pan-Africanism, Black consciousness, anticolonial struggle, agrarian collectivization and self-reliance against neocolonialism and racism.

nodes.name: Kropotkinian Anarchism
nodes.desc: Current of Peter Kropotkin that sees mutual aid as a law of nature and proposes federated communes, integration of farming and industry, science serving all and an ethics of solidarity without the state.

nodes.name: Confederate Conservatism
nodes.desc: Political tradition of the nineteenth-century American South tied to the Confederacy, defending states' rights and secession, an agrarian, patriarchal and Christian society, free trade and a military tradition. Historically, this tradition also defended slavery and racial hierarchy.

nodes.name: Agrarian Socialism
nodes.desc: Current that builds socialism from the countryside, with a single party, collectivization into villages and cooperatives, food self-sufficiency and protection of land and forests, as in Nyerere's Ujamaa.

nodes.name: Futurism
nodes.desc: Movement of Filippo Marinetti that exalted speed, machines, industry and war as the world's hygiene, preaching nationalism, anticlericalism and a break with the past, and that helped found Italian fascism.

nodes.name: Caesarism
nodes.desc: Roman imperial tradition that, from Julius Caesar through Augustus, Nero, Marcus Aurelius and Justinian, concentrates army, law and administration in the ruler while preserving institutions, popular provisioning and sovereignty over a diverse empire.

nodes.name: Industrial Capitalism
nodes.desc: Capitalism of the great industrialists such as Henry Ford, Rockefeller and Thomas Edison, exalting the factory, mass production, invention and the entrepreneur, with a work ethic, traditional family and minimal state interference.

nodes.name: Authoritarian Neoliberalism
nodes.desc: Regime that introduces radical free-market policies under a military dictatorship, with privatizations, trade opening and Chicago School economists, restricting unions, parties and opponents in the name of order and anticommunism.

nodes.name: Universalist Catholicism
nodes.desc: Christian vision that places the universal Church above nations, races and borders, in the line of Paul of Tarsus and Augustine, joining intense faith, traditional morals and spiritual authority with brotherhood among all peoples.

nodes.name: Confederal Republicanism
nodes.desc: Tradition of republics made of sovereign provinces or cantons, such as the Dutch Republic and the old Swiss Confederacy, with local self-government, open trade, armed neutrality and deep-rooted Protestant faith.

nodes.name: Anarcho-primitivism
nodes.desc: Current of John Zerzan and Ted Kaczynski that sees industrial civilization and agriculture itself as the root of domination, calling for the end of modern technology and a return to small stateless hunter-gatherer communities.

nodes.name: Federalist Socialism
nodes.desc: Model of a federation of socialist republics under a vanguard party, as in Lenin's USSR, combining a planned economy and single-party rule with national autonomy, local languages and cultures, and federated republics with a formal right to secede.

nodes.name: Patriotic Socialism
nodes.desc: Current that joins a state-run socialist economy and a strong party with patriotism, the traditional family, religion as national heritage and rejection of cultural progressivism, seeing identity politics as a liberal distraction from class struggle.

nodes.name: Vietnamese Socialism
nodes.desc: Model of the Communist Party of Vietnam uniting Ho Chi Minh Thought, anticolonial national liberation and the 1986 Đổi Mới: single-party rule, a socialist-oriented market economy, a dominant state sector and openness to global trade.

nodes.name: Ba'athist Socialism
nodes.desc: An Arab current of state socialism combining pan-Arab nationalism, a vanguard party, planning, land reform and control of strategic sectors, advocating Arab unity, secularism and independence from imperialism.

nodes.name: Islamism
nodes.desc: Political movement advocating a state governed by sharia and Islamic identity, born with Hassan al-Banna's and Sayyid Qutb's Muslim Brotherhood, combining mass activism, religious social welfare and rejection of Western secularism.

nodes.name: Islamic Democracy
nodes.desc: Current reconciling Islam with electoral democracy through conservative religious parties that run in elections and support a market economy and Muslim values in public life, like Turkey's early AKP and Tunisia's Ennahda.

nodes.name: Islamic Socialism
nodes.desc: Current grounding socialism in Islamic principles such as zakat, the ban on usury and Quranic social justice, combining anti-imperialism with a state-run economy, from Gaddafi's Third Universal Theory to Ali Shariati's thought.

nodes.name: Pan-Islamism
nodes.desc: Ideology advocating the political unity of Muslims above national borders, around the ummah and the ideal of a caliphate, formulated by Jamal al-Din al-Afghani and adopted by Ottoman sultan Abdul Hamid II against European colonialism.

nodes.name: Kemalist Nationalism
nodes.desc: Doctrine of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk that founded modern Turkey on six arrows: republicanism, nationalism, populism, statism, laicism and reformism, imposing Westernization and state control of religion from above.

nodes.name: Islamic Liberalism
nodes.desc: Reformist current that reinterprets Islam in light of reason, human rights and pluralism, advocating democracy, gender equality, a non-confessional state and freedom of conscience, in Muhammad Abduh's modernist tradition.

nodes.name: Buddhist Nationalism
nodes.desc: Current that joins ethnic identity and Theravada Buddhist faith and sees the nation as guardian of the Dharma, wary of the influence of other communities, as in Sinhalese nationalism in Sri Lanka and monk movements such as Ma Ba Tha and 969 in Myanmar.

nodes.name: Zionism
nodes.desc: Jewish national movement created by Herzl in 1897 that led to the State of Israel in 1948. It spans labor, revisionist and religious currents and today is expressed in a parliamentary democracy with strong military defense and a Law of Return.

nodes.name: Labor Zionism
nodes.desc: The socialist strand of Zionism that built the State of Israel through the kibbutzim, the Histadrut labor federation, and Ben-Gurion's Mapai party, uniting Jewish nationalism, collective work on the land, and a secular welfare state.

nodes.name: Feudalism
nodes.desc: A medieval order based on personal bonds of vassalage between lord and vassals, with land granted as fiefs, a hereditary warrior nobility, serfs bound to the land, the Church as moral authority, and power fragmented among local lords.

nodes.name: Carlist Traditionalism
nodes.desc: A Spanish current of counter-revolutionary traditionalism, born in the 19th-century Carlist Wars under the motto God, Fatherland, Fueros and King, advocating a legitimist Catholic monarchy, religious unity, regional fueros and an organic society against liberalism.

nodes.name: Clerical Fascism
nodes.desc: A variant of fascism that fuses ultranationalism, a mass party and militias with the authority of a national Church, with clergy in power, as in Dollfuss's Austrofascism, Father Tiso's Slovakia, the Croatian Ustaše and Romania's Iron Guard.

nodes.name: Islamic Theocratism
nodes.desc: A doctrine that hands the state to the Islamic clergy and makes sharia the supreme law, above popular sovereignty, as in Khomeini's guardianship of the jurist (velayat-e faqih) in Iran and the Taliban emirate in Afghanistan.

nodes.name: Blanquist Socialism
nodes.desc: Auguste Blanqui's doctrine that a conspiratorial revolutionary minority should seize power and rule through a provisional dictatorship that expropriates the bourgeoisie, with militant atheism and distrust of elections and of spontaneous mass action.

nodes.name: Buddhist Socialism
nodes.desc: A current that grounds socialism in Buddhist ethics, seeing compassion and the end of attachment as the basis of equality, common property and the rejection of caste, from Ambedkar and the Dalai Lama to Ne Win's Burmese socialism.

nodes.name: Buddhist Theocracy
nodes.desc: Rule by a Buddhist monastic hierarchy, with reincarnated leaders and monasteries dominating politics and land, traditional order and moral precepts as law, as in the Tibet of the Dalai Lama before 1950.

nodes.name: Enlightened Monarchism
nodes.desc: Enlightened absolutism: a sovereign monarch who rules by reason, "everything for the people, nothing by the people", with a bureaucracy of experts, education and reforms against the Church and the nobility, from Frederick II to Joseph II.

nodes.name: Jewish Theocracy
nodes.desc: Government ruled by the Torah and halakha, with rabbinical courts, judges or kings under religious authority, Judaism as the state religion and rejection of assimilation, inspired by the biblical kingdoms of Israel and Judah.

nodes.name: Municipalism
nodes.desc: A world divided into independent city-states and microstates that compete like a market, with free secession, the right of exit and political experimentation, from the medieval free cities to Yarvin's "patchwork" and seasteading.

nodes.name: Council Communism
nodes.desc: An anti-Leninist Marxist current of Pannekoek, Gorter and Mattick, which holds that workers themselves should run production and power through workers' councils, rejecting the vanguard party, the state and parliamentarism.

nodes.name: Democratic Confederalism
nodes.desc: A bottom-up self-government model of Abdullah Öcalan, with local assemblies federated into a confederation, ecology, gender equality and a cooperative economy, without a nation-state, put into practice in Rojava.

nodes.name: Traditionalism
nodes.desc: A current of René Guénon and Julius Evola that sees modernity as the decay of a universal spiritual tradition, defending sacred hierarchy, castes, initiatory order and the primacy of spirit over economics and mass politics.

nodes.name: Effective Accelerationism
nodes.desc: A movement born online in 2022 that argues for accelerating AI, energy and innovation through the market and without regulation, treating technological progress as a moral imperative and rejecting advocates of slowing down.

nodes.name: Direct Democracy
nodes.desc: A system in which citizens decide laws directly through referendums, popular initiatives, assemblies and recall of officials, instead of delegating to representatives, as in the Swiss cantons and classical Athens.

nodes.name: Dark Enlightenment
nodes.desc: Intellectual current of Nick Land and Curtis Yarvin that criticizes democracy, egalitarianism and the academic-media "Cathedral", defends autocratic governments and the right of exit, and includes accelerationist strands. Critics also associate it with so-called race realism.

nodes.name: Neocameralism
nodes.desc: A doctrine of Curtis Yarvin that proposes running the state as a joint-stock company: shareholders, a sovereign CEO, citizens as customers who can leave, guaranteed private property and politics replaced by management.

nodes.name: Tridemism
nodes.desc: Sun Yat-sen's republican doctrine, articulated in the Three Principles of the People: nationalism, democracy, and the people's livelihood. Its program envisioned transitional political tutelage, popular sovereignty, and social and economic reforms.

nodes.name: Postmodernism
nodes.desc: A plural critique of universalism, linear progress, and grand narratives. In a Foucauldian reading, genealogy and power/knowledge analysis show how institutions, norms, and discourses produce subjects and open possibilities for local resistance.

nodes.name: Chinese Socialism
nodes.desc: 21st-century doctrine of the CPC associated with Xi Jinping. It combines centralized Party leadership and socialist modernization, advocating national rejuvenation, predominant public ownership, and a socialist market with private enterprise and technological innovation.

nodes.name: Left-Wing Nationalism
nodes.desc: Combines national self-determination and popular sovereignty with social equality and left-wing economic policies. Its historical expressions range from anticolonial and socialist to developmentalist movements, without a single economic or institutional program.

nodes.name: Right-Wing Nationalism
nodes.desc: Prioritizes national sovereignty, identity, and cohesion, associating them with right-wing positions such as social hierarchy, cultural conservatism, or immigration restriction. Currents vary in their views of the state and economy, from free markets to national protectionism.

nodes.name: Machiavellian Republicanism
nodes.desc: A republican current inspired by Machiavelli’s Discourses on Livy. It defends civic liberty through laws, popular participation, and regulated conflict among social groups, allowing exceptional measures to preserve the republic.

nodes.name: Eurocommunism
nodes.desc: A 1970s Western European communist current that sought a national path to socialism through elections, party pluralism and civil liberties, independent of Moscow, with a mixed economy under democratic planning.

nodes.name: Internationalism
nodes.desc: Political doctrine advocating solidarity and cooperation among nations, overcoming nationalism, and strengthening global institutions for shared peace and development.

nodes.name: Internationalist Socialism
nodes.desc: Branch of socialism advocating the global unity of working people against capitalism, rejecting bourgeois nationalism, and defending international working-class solidarity.

nodes.name: Internationalist Democracy
nodes.desc: Doctrine proposing a democratic and federated global political order where citizens and nations deliberate jointly through multilateral representative institutions and lawful cooperation.

nodes.name: Georgism
nodes.desc: Economic philosophy founded by Henry George holding that natural resources and land belong to the whole community, advocating a single land value tax (LVT) and the abolition of taxes on labor and capital.

nodes.name: Geosocialism
nodes.desc: Synthesis of Georgism and socialism advocating the socialization of economic rent from land and natural monopolies to fund universal public services and a citizen dividend.

nodes.name: Georgist Distributism
nodes.desc: Fusion of distributism and Georgism promoting widespread family ownership of productive property combined with land value taxation to prevent monopolies and state collectivism.

nodes.name: Malthusianism
nodes.desc: Doctrine inspired by Malthus that proposes curbing population growth through late marriage, education and family responsibility, replacing poor relief with work incentives and protecting property and national agriculture.

nodes.name: Neo-Malthusianism
nodes.desc: Current that proposes tackling population pressure on resources through contraception, voluntary family planning, sex education and women's reproductive autonomy, backed by public health and development.

nodes.name: Anarcho-Monarchism
nodes.desc: Syncretic doctrine that proposes the abolition of the state while retaining a traditional monarch without coercive power, serving as a symbol of unity, voluntary arbiter, and guardian of order against tyranny.

nodes.name: Techno-Progressivism
nodes.desc: Democratic transhumanism combining public oversight of technology with social justice, defending human enhancement, radical life extension, morphological freedom and universal sharing of the gains from automation.

nodes.name: Rioplatense Federalism
nodes.desc: Río de la Plata federalist tradition founded by José Gervasio Artigas in the League of the Free Peoples (1813–1820). It advocates republican confederalism of sovereign provinces against Buenos Aires centralism, civil and religious liberty, tariff protection, and popular land reform.

nodes.name: Vitalism
nodes.desc: Current that takes life itself, Bergson's élan vital and Nietzsche's will to power, as the supreme value, exalting instinct, physical vigor, creation and heroism against decadence, sickness and egalitarianism.

nodes.name: British Fascism
nodes.desc: The fascism of Oswald Mosley and the British Union of Fascists: a single leader, Blackshirts and a corporate state, with an autarkic empire, British nationalism, antisemitism and opposition to liberalism and communism.

nodes.name: Techno-Feudalism
nodes.desc: Current that sees in the power of platforms and big technology companies a new feudal order and defends it: a mosaic of sovereign corporate fiefs where the owner of the cloud governs vassals and users and lives off rent, not competition.

nodes.name: Pragmatic Liberalism
nodes.desc: Liberalism that defends democracy, individual rights and a market economy, but tests each policy against evidence: it accepts regulation, a safety net and targeted intervention when they fix market failures, as in Clinton's Third Way.

nodes.name: Pragmatic Conservatism
nodes.desc: Conservatism that protects institutions, family and order without doctrinal rigidity: it allows gradual reform and concessions in order to conserve the essential, in the line of Burke and Disraeli, rather than restoring an idealized past.

nodes.name: Colonialism
nodes.desc: System in which a metropole rules distant territories and peoples to settle them and extract wealth, imposing an exclusive trade pact, compulsory labor and hierarchy under the pretext of a civilizing or religious mission.

nodes.name: Developmentalism
nodes.desc: Current that seeks to overcome underdevelopment through accelerated industrialization, state planning, public infrastructure, protection of infant industry and a partnership between the state, national capital and foreign capital, as in Kubitschek's Targets Plan.

nodes.name: Conservative Social Democracy
nodes.desc: Current that keeps the welfare state, trade unions and mixed economy, but defends family, nation, public order and restricted immigration, as in Mette Frederiksen's Danish social democracy.

nodes.name: Austrofascism
nodes.desc: Authoritarian, corporatist, Catholic regime of Dollfuss and Schuschnigg (1934–1938): single party (Fatherland Front), a Ständestaat inspired by Quadragesimo Anno, repression of socialists and Nazis, and defense of a German, Christian, independent Austria.

nodes.name: Enlightenment
nodes.desc: Eighteenth-century European intellectual movement that champions reason, science and tolerance against superstition and absolutism, with natural rights, separation of powers, education and progress as the basis of society.
